newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Imax sees speedup in Asia deals.
newsitem.headline: Imax sees speedup in Asia deals.

text.p: Giant screen and three-dimensional (3-D) theatre company Imax Corp sees Asia as its fastest growing market, with more deals coming from the region at a faster rate over the past year, a senior company official said on Friday.
"We think Asia-Pacific will be the fastest growing market for the company in the world," Richard Gelfond, vice chairman and chief executive officer, told Reuters in an interview.

"There were 12 theatres in Asia-Pacific, excluding Japan, in the 29-year history of the company. We've had our office in Singapore for one year and we've signed six theatres so far since we opened the office, excluding Japan.

"We acquired the company in 1993. Before that time the baseline for the company was 12 signings a year. In the next few years we expect Asia-Pacific to be able to do 10 (theatre) systems a year. And we're not far from that," he said.
Gelfond said it usually took a year for a contract to be signed from the initial indication of interest.
"But with the commercial people in Asia, the cycle seems to be a lot shorter. So the deal we just signed in Malaysia, we've been talking to them for around six months."

On Thursday, Imax announced it had signed an agreement with Malaysia's PhileoLand Berhad to install two 3-D theatres and two Ridefilm motion simulator systems over the next three years, with an option for a third theatre. The first theatre would open in early 1998.
It also signed a deal with Taiwan's Kings Entertainment Company for up to three theatres. The two deals would give Imax revenues of US$15 to $40 million in cash and royalties.
Gelfond said Imax could secure up to five more theatre deals in the region before the end of this year.
The opening of two new theatres in Sydney and Tokyo later this month and in early October would further spur its growth momentum in the region, he said.
Gelfond said what was stoking interest in Imax's theatre systems and simulator Ridefilms was the increasing level of disposable income and the demand for family type entertainment.

"Asia is experiencing the same trend (as) in the rest of the world towards location-based entertainment, which is a bundling of different types of attractions which typically includes multiplex cinemas, restaurants, theme shopping and an Imax theatre in one location that people go to be entertained," he said.
Imax also is exploring ways to capture the less developed markets in Asia, like China.
Gelfond said the company has had discussions with Asian investors about investing in Imax products in China.

"We have about two dozen real inquiries that we are following up on. Over time, we will make inroads into China. I would be surprised if we didn't announce a theatre in China in the next year or two," he said.
